webpage.text:
The inspiration for Frankenstein? | Environment

Heading for the Quantocks, we went through the heart of the levels, crossing the river Parrett below the sudden conical hill called Burrow Mump, and passing close by King Alfred's Athelney. Then, skirting Taunton, we came to the narrow lanes, deep-red sandstone buildings and thickly wooded hillsides that characterise the Quantocks. We found Broomfield, highest of the Quantock villages, and an estate there with wild woodland glades, ponds and rhododendrons in bloom across the slopes. Down beyond a folly with two round castellated towers was a wide opening with a lawn and courtyard bordered by stone buildings – remains of the mansion of Fyne Court, home for centuries of the Crosse family, but burnt down in 1894.

To our right, opposite a bell tower and outbuildings, stood one substantial wing of the mansion still intact. In one of the outbuildings, a display of photographs and drawings showed the mansion as it had once been, indicating that this surviving wing had housed the music room where, some 200 years ago, Andrew Crosse ("the wizard of Broomfield") had built his experimental electrical equipment. It was from here that he slung a copper wire to posts across the hillside as a conductor for storm lightning. And he stated his belief that by the agency of electricity "we shall be enabled to communicate our thoughts instantaneously with the uttermost parts of the earth". But it was his experimental attempts to create silicate crystals that led to his becoming the object of local wonder. He reported that what seemed to be tiny insects appeared to materialise from rocks to which he had applied an electrical charge. The word spread that he had created life and the legend grew that here, in his Somerset estate, Crosse was the inspiration for Mary Shelley's Frankenstein and his monstrous creation.

webpage.text:
Fyne Court near Bridgewater

Explore the wild garden and discover where the ‘Thunder and Lightning Man’ lived.

Beautiful snowdrops and bluebells in the Spring.

There are several walks through the woods, clearly but unobtrusively marked by posts.

The Walled Garden is currently being restored while the Mill Pond is a great place to see dragonfly, toad and other wildlife.

Don’t miss the twin-towered Folly which adds to the Gothic mood of fear, anxiety and horror.

Fyne Court is also the headquarters of the Somerset Wildlife Trust.

National Trust members visit for free.

Family friendly Archives - Page 9 of 25

Erddig House and Garden

Wrexham, Wrexham County Borough, LL13 0YT

A remarkable example of an early 18th century formal walled garden. Based on a central axis, the canal is flanked by formal lawns and apple orchards, divided by pleached lime avenues. Fruit trees are espaliered against the surrounding high walls.

Exbury

Southampton, Hampshire, SO45 1AZ

Exbury Gardens lie on the edge of the New Forest near Southampton. It has a spectacular collection of woodland gardens as well as herbaceous, contemporary and wildflower gardens.

Fast Rabbit Farm Gardens

Dartmouth, Devon, TQ6 0NB

Fast Rabbit Farm near Dartmouth is set in two adjoining valleys with a lake and several ponds. The valley sides have wide contoured grass walks with an abundance of wild flowers and wild life. Plantings include rhododendron, camellia and magnolia underplanted with thousands of bulbs.

Felbrigg Hall Gardens

Norwich, Norfolk, NR11 8PR

Felbrigg Hall near Norwich dates back to the Tudor period. The surrounding gardens include a stunning Walled Garden with herbaceous borders, orchard, vegetable and herb borders.

Felley Priory

Nottingham, Nottinghamshire, NG16 5FJ

Felley Priory, just off the M1 near Nottingham, is a garden for all seasons. Discover many rare and unusual plants in the 2.5 acre garden that surrounds the Tudor manor house.

Fenton House

London, London, NW3 6SP

Fenton House in Hampstead, is a beautiful 17th century merchant house with a Walled Garden.

Forde Abbey

Chard, Somerset, TA20 4LU

Forde Abbey near Chard has a rich and interesting history. The stunning gardens continue to evolve and include herbaceous borders, lakes and a bog garden.

Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal Water Garden

Ripon, North Yorkshire, HG4 3DY

Fountains Abbey and Studley Royal Water Gardens are near Ripon. Beautiful 12th century Abbey ruins with one of the most magnificent Georgian water gardens ever created.

Franciscan Gardens Canterbury

Canterbury, Kent, CT1 2BD

Escape the bustle of Canterbury city centre and relax in the recently replanted Franciscan Gardens. Inspired by the site's original use as a Franciscan Friary, discover a hidden gem of symbolic planting, peaceful paths and the beautiful Greyfriars Chapel.

Fullers Mill

Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk, IP28 6HD

Fullers Mill is an enchanting and tranquil seven-acre garden created by the late Bernard Tickner MBE. It combines light dappled woodland with a plantsman’s collection of shrubs, perennials, lilies and marginal plants enhanced by the reflective cooling waters of the River Lark, Millpond and Culford Stream.

Fursdon House Gardens

Exeter, Devon, EX5 5JS

Home of the Fursdon family since 1259, Fursdon House is surrounded by 4 acres of hillside gardens which have been extensively restored and replanted over the last 40 years.

Fyne Court

Bridgwater, Somerset, TA5 2EQ

Hidden in the Quantock Hills near Bridgwater, is Fyne Court. Blizzards of snowdrops in February are followed by drifts of bluebells in the woods surrounding the property.
